title: Fix live Print Queue pg-boss transaction freeze and add worker-aware health/recovery

acceptanceCriteria.description: The production Print Queue consumer uses a dedicated Supabase session-mode port-5432 connection, while the API remains a producer and transaction-pooler port 6543 is rejected for long-lived worker consumption.

Repeated statement/idle-transaction timeouts, sustained clock skew, stale heartbeat, stale claims, and stale durable progress fail health and request a controlled restart instead of remaining falsely live.
Persisted worker heartbeat/job state and /health/deep distinguish Print Queue list counts from pg-boss claims, durable batch progress, provider state, and worker liveness.
Recovery admits only the current generation after a generation-matched durable write, fences stale payloads, and blocks automatic replay whenever a provider outcome is unknown.

The nine historical provider-pending sidecars were reconciled only after rollback-only proof of nine durable provider receipts and zero unresolved purchase intents; six now reference existing queue entries, three record shipment persistence, repeat execution is a no-op, and no provider call or job replay occurred.

Production /health/deep changed from HTTP 503 provider_reconciliation_required to HTTP 200 ready with a fresh heartbeat, zero pg-boss work, zero active durable jobs, and zero provider-pending sidecars.
The focused and adjacent worker/lifecycle/lockdown suites, all 45 source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and the production frontend build pass at the reviewed SHA.

Shipped/cancelled locks and label-purchase protections were not weakened; closure updated only nine Print Queue item sidecars and performed zero order/shipment writes, label purchase/void, postage charge, marketplace notification, inventory movement, provider invocation, or manual service restart.

sotBypass.details: The worker and durable job store remain authoritative. Health only reads their facts. The operator tool cannot invoke a provider or replay a job and changes sidecar state only when the canonical shipment receipt, inactive-job, exact-incident, and unresolved-intent guards all pass.

evidence.proves: A migrated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture detects a stale durable/pg-boss lifecycle, atomically increments recovery generation, rejects a stale generation write, admits the current generation, and returns healthy after terminal progress.

Production rejects missing or transaction-pooler consumer URLs; old and current recovery payloads admit one provider boundary, stale writes have zero effect, and provider-pending state blocks automatic recovery.

Injected statement/idle-transaction timeouts, clock skew, stale durable state, provider-accepted/local-sidecar-loss, and overlapping recovery generations fail closed, request restart only for infrastructure faults, and reconcile without a second provider effect.

The exact bounded SQL reconciles an incident-shaped nine-sidecar fixture to six queued and three shipment-persisted states only from durable receipts; the repeat run fails the incident guard and updates zero.

evidence.command: Rollback-only preflight, then npx tsx scripts/ps-430-reconcile-provider-pending.ts --apply --expected-count=9, followed by a READ ONLY aggregate query and GET /health/deep.
evidence.proves: Production matched the exact nine/eight/three incident guard, committed nine sidecar-only transitions, then reported zero pending items and HTTP 200 ready worker health with zero active/retry work.
The policy/placement guard and executable migrated-database connection, liveness, timeout, generation, provider-pending, and reconciliation proof run together.

evidence.proves: All 45 mandatory source-of-truth, worker, label, inventory, billing, lifecycle, lockdown, and runtime-schema guards pass at the reviewed SHA.
Backend and frontend strict TypeScript checks pass.
The production frontend bundle builds successfully with 2,977 modules transformed.

The implementation is limited to dedicated worker connection/health/recovery fencing plus guarded sidecar-only operational closure. No enumerated lockdown file changed, and no order/shipment schema, edit lock, inventory switch, provider purchase owner, or frontend business authority was weakened.

verification.command: PS-430 adds no migration; it executes against migration-owned 0062 sidecars and verifies their schema with the focused migrated fixture.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No schema rollback is required. Revert the packet/closure commits and PS-430 implementation commit if application rollback is necessary; retain the nine reconciled sidecar states because they accurately describe already-durable provider receipts and reverting them would reintroduce false provider ambiguity.

rollback.strategy: Revert the packet commit, 0d5bd29ae17ce25672405bc60640cff84d795106, and 2e3a0011fe9cd7fb374f12a0b0f99ece01a3a61e before redeploying. Restore the previous worker start command only as an operator-approved configuration rollback. Do not restore provider_pending on the nine resolved sidecars, replay their jobs, delete shipment/queue history, or mutate shipped/cancelled orders.

liveVerification.reason: The dedicated worker is live on session-mode port 5432. An approved rollback-only preflight and guarded apply reconciled all nine known provider-success sidecars without provider or job execution. A read-only after-check reports zero provider-pending items, and /health/deep is HTTP 200 with fresh heartbeat and zero pg-boss/active durable work.
